extracted.intended_audience: Parties and counsel in PTAB post-grant review proceedings (petitioners, patent owners, patent litigators)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements for requesting rehearing of a PTAB Final Written Decision in a Post-Grant Review (PGR), including the petitioner's burden and specificity requirements under 37 C.F.R. § 42.71(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of persuasion to modify a decision
rubrics_metrics.description: “The burden of showing that a decision should be modified lies with the party challenging the decision.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited from the Office Patent Trial Practice Guide (77 Fed. Reg. 48,756, 48,768 (Aug. 14, 2012)). A party seeking rehearing must carry the burden of demonstrating why the Board's decision should be changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearing specificity requirement (37 C.F.R. § 42.71(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: In its request for rehearing, the dissatisfied party must (1) “specifically identify all matters the party believes the Board misapprehended or overlooked” and (2) identify the place “where each matter was previously addressed.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for rehearing that do not specifically identify alleged misapprehensions/oversights and point to where those matters were previously raised will fail to meet the regulatory requirement. See Office Patent Trial Practice Guide, 77 Fed. Reg. at 48,768.

rubrics_metrics.name: PGR unpatentability standard — 'more likely than not'
rubrics_metrics.description: To prevail on an obviousness (or other) ground in PGR, the petitioner must show that it is more likely than not that the challenged claim is unpatentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Written Decision evaluated petitioner's obviousness grounds against the 'more likely than not' standard; failure to meet that threshold means the petitioner did not establish unpatentability. Demonstrating underlying factual predicates (e.g., prior art status) is necessary to meet this standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art status requirement for obviousness grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: An obviousness ground depends on the contention that cited references constitute prior art; the petitioner must show sufficiently that those references are prior art against the challenged patent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the petitioner does not satisfactorily establish that a reference is prior art (e.g., Board found Petitioner failed to show Varenna 2016 and Manara are prior art), the obviousness ground will fail. Reliance on alternative primary references (e.g., Varenna 2012) must be properly identified and considered.
